To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
calcium is necessary for catecholamine release from the adrenal glands of the cat.

The adrenal glands of cats, perfused with Locke’s solution, secrete catecholamines in response to muscarine, histamine, serotonin, angiotensins and bradykinins; that these responses are abolished when the perfusion medium does not contain calcium ions; and that these responses are not inhibited by atropine, but are abolished by hexamethonium.

the following substances evoked secretion of catecholamines from perfused cat adrenal glands: muscarine and related agents (pilocarpine, methocholine, acetylcholine, nicotine); 5-hydroxtryptamine; histamine; and bradykinins and related polypeptides (angiotensin).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of catecholamine release from the adrenal medulla.
the mechanism of adrenomedullary secretion evoked by drugs.
the mechanism whereby catecholamine release from the adrenal glands of the cat is evoked by biogenic amines, polypeptides and muscarinic drugs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the secretion of catecholamines from the adrenal medulla is dependent upon the presence of calcium in the perfusion medium and that this is the case for the action of all the drugs tested.
the catecholamine-releasing effect of the following agents is mediated by calcium: acetylcholine, nicotine, and muscarine.

the adrenal medullary secretion of adrenaline and noradrenaline is dependent on the presence of calcium in the perfusing medium, and that this is true for the secretion of these catecholamines by all the drugs so far tested, namely, acetylcholine, nicotine, histamine, and 5-hydrotryptamine, bradykinin, angiotensins I and II, and the polypeptides substance P and physalaemin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
calcium is a necessary factor for secretion evoked by a variety of agents, and that the effect of these substances is to increase calcium influx.
the adrenal gland is a useful tool to study the mechanism by which drugs promote the release of catecholamines from storage sites.
the secretion of epinephrine and norepinephrine from the adrenal glands of cats and dogs is dependent on calcium.
The main takeaway from our work is that
calcium is necessary for secretion evoked by all of these agents.
calcium is required for the secretion of catecholamines evoked by a wide variety of drugs.
calcium is required in the secretory process of the adrenal medulla.
